# Cape Vows — SEO Audit

*Generated by `/seo audit` · 2026-06-15 · Target: https://capevows.co.za*

**Method note:** This audit is grounded in the **live served HTML** (what crawlers and AI engines actually receive over HTTP, before JavaScript runs), the **live `robots.txt`**, the **sitemap**, and the **actual source** (`index.html`, `src/App.jsx`, `vercel.json`, `public/`). For a client-rendered SPA the served HTML and the rendered DOM differ sharply, and most of the highest-impact findings live in that gap — a black-box external crawl alone would miss them. Field data requiring external APIs (CrUX/PageSpeed field CWV, live SERP positions, GSC impressions) was **not** available in this environment and is reasoned about, not measured — flagged inline where relevant.

**Business type:** Publisher / niche directory (Western Cape wedding venues). Not local-business (no single GBP storefront), not e-commerce. GEO/AI-citation is an explicit stated goal (per `CLAUDE.md`, `AUDIT.md`).

The number is mid-range for a reason: **the foundations are competent, but three structural issues cap the entire surface.** Fix the three Criticals and this is a 75+ site without touching the content.

---

## Executive Summary

Cape Vows is a well-built directory sitting behind three doors that are currently shut.

**Door 1 — AI engines are told to stay out.** The live `robots.txt` (Cloudflare's "Managed / Block AI bots" feature) explicitly `Disallow: /`s `GPTBot`, `ClaudeBot`, `Google-Extended`, `CCBot`, `Bytespider`, `meta-externalagent`, `Amazonbot`, and `Applebot-Extended`, and sets `Content-Signal: ai-train=no`. For a site whose **stated differentiation is AI/GEO citation**, this is self-defeating — and it's the exact same class of problem as the Bot Fight Mode warning already in `CLAUDE.md`, one toggle over.

**Door 2 — every page claims to be the homepage.** The SPA updates `document.title` and the meta description per route, but **never updates the canonical tag or the Open Graph tags.** So all 24 venue pages, 5 blog posts, and `/venues` ship `<link rel="canonical" href="https://capevows.co.za">` — telling Google they are duplicates of the homepage. This is an active indexing risk for the entire money surface.

**Door 3 — the content only exists after JavaScript runs.** Confirmed live: `https://capevows.co.za/venues/babylonstoren` serves the **identical homepage `<title>`** at the HTTP level. Per-page titles, descriptions, H1s, body copy, and all JSON-LD are injected client-side. Googlebot renders JS (eventually), but social scrapers and most AI crawlers do not — so shares look generic and AI engines that *do* visit get an empty shell.

The good news: doors 2 and 3 share one key. A **build-time prerender** (e.g. `react-snap` or a Vite SSG/prerender step — additive, no framework swap, no splitting `App.jsx`) emits real per-route HTML and fixes canonical, OG, titles, meta, body content, *and* JSON-LD visibility in a single move. Door 1 is a Cloudflare dashboard toggle. None of this requires rewriting the app.

---

## CRITICAL

### C1 — `robots.txt` blocks every major AI crawler *(GEO / Technical · effort: minutes)*
- **Observation (first principle):** An AI engine cannot cite what it is contractually told not to fetch. The live `robots.txt` is Cloudflare-managed and contains explicit `Disallow: /` blocks for `GPTBot`, `ClaudeBot`, `Google-Extended`, `CCBot`, `Bytespider`, `meta-externalagent`, `Amazonbot`, `Applebot-Extended`, plus `Content-Signal: ai-train=no` on `User-agent: *`.
- **Impact:** ChatGPT, Claude, Gemini (grounding/training via Google-Extended), and Common Crawl (which feeds many LLMs) are all excluded. Bing/Copilot and Perplexity aren't explicitly blocked but are then limited by Door 3 (CSR).
- **Why it matters:** Your entire GEO thesis (cited as the strategic edge in `AUDIT.md` and `CLAUDE.md`) depends on these exact bots. Regular Google/Bing *search* is unaffected (`search=yes`, `Allow: /`), so this is purely an AI-citation loss — but that's the upside you're chasing.
- **Dependency (unblocks):** Prerequisite for **C3**'s GEO payoff and for any llms.txt / AI-citation work (M3). No point optimising for AI citation while the front door says no.
- **Fix:** In Cloudflare → disable the **"Block AI Scrapers and Crawlers" / AI Audit** managed `robots.txt` feature (or override `robots.txt` with your own that `Allow`s the AI agents you want). Decide deliberately per bot — at minimum allow `GPTBot`, `ClaudeBot`, `Google-Extended`, `PerplexityBot`, `CCBot`.
- **Falsifiability (how you'd know it failed):** After the change, `curl https://capevows.co.za/robots.txt` should no longer show `Disallow: /` under those agents. If it still does, the managed feature re-injected it.
- **Leading indicator to monitor:** Server-log hits from `GPTBot`/`ClaudeBot`/`Google-Extended` user-agents appearing within 1–2 weeks; later, brand mentions when querying ChatGPT/Perplexity for "Western Cape wedding venues."
- **Caveat:** If blocking AI is a *deliberate* content-protection choice, then the honest move is to drop the GEO goal from the strategy docs — you can't hold both.

### C2 — Canonical tag is the homepage on every route *(On-Page · effort: solved by C3, or a small JS shim)*
- **Observation:** `index.html` ships a static `<link rel="canonical" href="https://capevows.co.za">`. A source grep confirms the SPA updates only `document.title` and `meta[name=description]` — **nothing updates the canonical** (or `og:url`). So `/venues/babylonstoren`, `/blog/...`, and `/venues` all declare the homepage as their canonical.
- **Impact:** Google treats a canonical as a strong "this page *is* that URL" signal. Declaring 32 distinct pages as canonical-to-homepage invites de-duplication — the venue and blog pages may be dropped from the index in favour of the homepage.
- **Why it matters:** The 24 venue pages + 5 blog posts *are* your long-tail ranking surface ("[Venue] wedding venue", "Franschhoek wine estate wedding"). A homepage canonical quietly works against every one of them.
- **Dependency:** Fully resolved by **C3** (prerender writes a correct per-route canonical). If C3 is deferred, a stop-gap is a small `useEffect` that rewrites the canonical `href` per route — but note that fix is still client-side (Googlebot-only).
- **Fix (preferred):** Prerender per-route HTML with the correct self-referential canonical + `og:url`. **Stop-gap:** update `<link rel="canonical">` and `og:url` in the same effects that already set the title.
- **Falsifiability:** `curl -s https://capevows.co.za/venues/babylonstoren | grep canonical` should show the venue URL, not the bare domain. Today it shows the homepage.
- **Leading indicator:** GSC → Pages → "Duplicate, Google chose different canonical" count should fall; venue URLs move to "Indexed."

### C3 — Client-side rendering hides content from non-JS crawlers *(Technical / GEO · effort: build step, no rewrite)*
- **Observation:** `vercel.json` rewrites `/(.*) → /index.html`; React injects all per-route content, meta, and JSON-LD at runtime. **Confirmed live:** the venue URL returns the homepage `<title>` and the homepage's generic description over HTTP.
- **Impact:** Googlebot renders JS (so it can index *eventually*, on a delayed second pass and a finite render budget), but **social scrapers and most AI crawlers never run JS** — they see an empty `#root` shell with homepage meta. This is the root cause behind C2, H2 (OG), and half of C1's damage.
- **Why it matters:** It simultaneously suppresses social/Pinterest sharing (H2), per-page canonical/meta (C2), and AI citability (C1) — one root, three symptoms.
- **Dependency (keystone):** Resolving C3 also resolves **C2** and **H2** and makes your existing rich JSON-LD (S1 below) visible without JS. Highest leverage technical change on the site.
- **Fix:** Add a **build-time prerender** that crawls the built SPA and emits static HTML per route — `react-snap`, `vite-plugin-prerender`, or Vercel's prerendering. This is **additive**: it keeps Vite, keeps the single-file `App.jsx`, swaps no framework, and violates none of the `CLAUDE.md` constraints. (Do **not** move to Next.js/SSR — that *would* breach the no-framework-swap rule.)
- **Falsifiability:** After prerender, `curl` of a venue URL shows the venue's own `<title>`, description, canonical, and inline JSON-LD with **no JS executed**. If it still shows the homepage shell, the prerender didn't cover that route.
- **Leading indicator:** GSC "Crawled — currently not indexed" should drop; rich-result eligibility for EventVenue/FAQ should appear in GSC's Enhancements without waiting on render.

## HIGH

### H1 — Soft 404s: every non-existent URL returns HTTP 200 *(Technical)*
- **Observation:** The catch-all rewrite means `curl /this-page-does-not-exist-12345` → **HTTP 200** + `index.html`. The `NotFound` component is client-only; the status code is never 404. (`/llms.txt` returning "200" is the same artifact — it's the shell, not a real file.)
- **Why it matters:** Crawlers rely on status codes. Infinite 200-returning junk URLs waste crawl budget and can trigger Google's soft-404 heuristics, which are noisier than an honest 404.
- **Fix:** Serve a real 404 for unmatched routes. With the SPA + Vercel, the clean options are (a) prerender a `404.html` and let Vercel return it with a 404 status for unmatched paths, or (b) keep the rewrite but ensure genuinely invalid venue/blog slugs emit a `<meta name="robots" content="noindex">` at minimum. Prerendering (C3) makes (a) natural.
- **Falsifiability:** `curl -I` of a garbage URL returns `404`, not `200`.
- **Leading indicator:** GSC → "Soft 404" report trends to zero.

### H2 — Open Graph / Twitter tags are the homepage on every share *(On-Page / Social)*
- **Observation:** `og:title`, `og:url`, `og:description`, `og:image`, and all `twitter:*` are static in `index.html` and never updated by JS. Every shared venue/blog URL renders the **same generic homepage card**.
- **Why it matters:** Sharing is core to this product — couples send venue links to a partner; **the Pinterest launch (11 pins) is a pending `CLAUDE.md` item** and depends entirely on per-URL OG/image. Social scrapers never run JS, so this is unfixable client-side.
- **Dependency:** Resolved by **C3** (prerender writes per-route OG). Until then, Pinterest/WhatsApp/FB shares of any deep link are generic.
- **Fix:** Per-route OG tags via prerender; ideally a venue-specific `og:image` once photography lands (ties to `AUDIT.md` S1).
- **Falsifiability:** Facebook Sharing Debugger / `curl … | grep og:title` on a venue URL shows the venue name, not the homepage title.
- **Leading indicator:** Pinterest/Facebook link previews show venue-specific titles & images; referral sessions from Pinterest in GA4.

### H3 — AI-citation completeness: `ai-train=no`, no `llms.txt`, content invisible *(GEO)*
- **Observation:** Beyond C1's hard blocks, `Content-Signal: ai-train=no` is set, there is **no real `llms.txt`** (the 200 is a soft-404 shell), and even non-blocked AI bots (Perplexity, Bing/Copilot) hit the CSR shell.
- **Why it matters:** These are the *secondary* GEO levers — they only pay off once C1 (unblock) and C3 (prerender) are done, but they complete the picture.
- **Dependency:** Do **after** C1 + C3.
- **Fix:** Once unblocked and prerendered, add a real `public/llms.txt` (curated index of venues + blog with one-line factual summaries — plays directly to your answer-first content). Reconsider `ai-train` signal in line with the GEO goal.
- **Falsifiability:** `curl /llms.txt` returns the curated text file, not HTML; AI engines begin returning Cape Vows venue facts when asked.
- **Leading indicator:** Manual monthly spot-checks in ChatGPT/Perplexity/Gemini for "best Franschhoek wedding venues" surfacing capevows.co.za.

## MEDIUM

### M1 — No `Sitemap:` directive in `robots.txt` *(Technical)*
`sitemap.xml` is valid and complete (33 URLs; all 24 venue slugs + 5 blog slugs verified against `App.jsx` — **zero mismatches**, good hygiene), but `robots.txt` doesn't reference it. **Fix:** add `Sitemap: https://capevows.co.za/sitemap.xml` (and submit in GSC + Bing Webmaster Tools). *Monitor:* GSC Sitemaps "Discovered URLs" = 33.

### M2 — Thin `/vendors` page is indexable and in the sitemap *(Content)*
`/vendors` is a "Coming Soon" placeholder (now with a "Soon" nav badge) but is in `sitemap.xml` at priority 0.7 and fully crawlable. **Fix:** either `noindex` it until it ships or drop it from the sitemap; re-add when real vendor content exists. *Falsifiable:* a thin-content/"Crawled — not indexed" flag on `/vendors` in GSC.

### M3 — Duplicate `WebSite` JSON-LD *(Schema)*
`index.html` ships a static `WebSite` schema, and `App.jsx` injects a second `WebSite` (with `SearchAction`) at runtime under `global-jsonld`. Two `WebSite` nodes is redundant and the `SearchAction` points at `/venues?q=` which isn't a real search endpoint. **Fix:** keep one `WebSite` (the prerendered/static one), and only keep `SearchAction` if `/venues?q=` actually filters (it now can, post the Batch-2 filters-in-URL work — verify the param name matches). *Monitor:* Rich Results Test shows a single WebSite entity.

### M4 — Blog posts lack author/`Person` schema and visible bylines *(E-E-A-T)*
`BlogPosting` is present but there's no `author` `Person`, no visible byline, no author bio. The new homepage founder note is good E-E-A-T but isn't connected to the posts. **Fix:** add `author` (Person, the founder) to `BlogPosting`, a small visible byline, and link to the founder note. *Why:* E-E-A-T "Experience/Authoritativeness" for YMYL-adjacent planning content. *Monitor:* author appears in Rich Results Test for blog URLs.

### M5 — `EventVenue` schema is thin *(Schema)*
Per-venue `EventVenue` has name/description/address/telephone/url but no `geo` (lat/lng), no `image`, no `maximumAttendeeCapacity`, no `priceRange`. **Fix:** add `geo` coordinates and `maximumAttendeeCapacity` (you already hold capacity data); add `image` once real photography exists (`AUDIT.md` S1). *Monitor:* richer entity in Rich Results Test; potential Place/Map features.

### M6 — Sitemap `lastmod` is static and uniform *(Technical)*
Every URL shows `2026-05-10` (≈5 weeks stale at audit date) regardless of actual change. Not harmful, but a missed freshness signal and slightly noisy. **Fix:** generate `lastmod` per-URL at build time from real content changes. *Monitor:* `lastmod` values diverge and track deploys.

## LOW / BACKLOG

- **L1 — CSS + fonts injected at runtime (render-blocking on the JS bundle).** `document.createElement` for the stylesheet and font link means first paint waits on the bundle. Preconnect was added (good). *Backlog:* ship critical CSS as a real `<link>`/inline block so first paint isn't JS-gated. (Largely moot once C3 prerenders.)
- **L2 — Blog images lack responsive `srcset`.** Unsplash heroes use fixed width params + lazy loading (alt text present — good). *Backlog:* add `srcset`/`sizes`; add `fetchpriority="high"` to the blog hero (LCP element).
- **L3 — Missing hardening headers.** HSTS is present (2yr); no CSP, `X-Content-Type-Options`, or `X-Frame-Options`. Minor for SEO, good hygiene. *Backlog:* add via `vercel.json` headers.
- **L4 — `FAQPage` schema (informational, no action).** Google retired FAQ rich results for all sites in **May 2026** — the per-venue `FAQPage` no longer yields a SERP feature. **Do not remove it:** it still aids AI/LLM citation (once C1+C3 are fixed). Flagged here only so the loss of the SERP feature isn't mistaken for a bug.

## Prioritised Action Plan (dependency-sequenced)

**Phase 1 — Open the doors (days, highest ROI)**
1. **C1** — Turn off Cloudflare's AI-bot block / fix `robots.txt`. *(Minutes. Unblocks the entire GEO thesis.)*
2. **M1** — Add `Sitemap:` to `robots.txt`; submit sitemap in GSC + Bing. *(Minutes.)*
3. **C3** — Stand up a build-time prerender (`react-snap` / Vite prerender). *(The keystone — also delivers C2 and H2.)*

**Phase 2 — Land the prerender payoff (after C3)**
4. **C2** — Verify per-route canonical + `og:url` are now correct in served HTML.
5. **H2** — Verify per-route OG/Twitter tags; wire up the Pinterest launch.
6. **H1** — Real 404 status for unmatched routes (`404.html` via prerender).
7. **M3** — De-duplicate `WebSite` JSON-LD; confirm `SearchAction` matches the real `/venues?` param.

**Phase 3 — Complete GEO + E-E-A-T (after Phases 1–2)**
8. **H3** — Add a real `llms.txt`; reconsider `ai-train` signal.
9. **M4** — Author `Person` schema + bylines linked to the founder note.
10. **M5** — Enrich `EventVenue` (geo, capacity; image when photography lands).
11. **M2 / M6 / L-series** — `noindex` thin `/vendors`, dynamic `lastmod`, headers, image `srcset`, critical CSS.

**Sequencing logic:** C1 and C3 are independent and can run in parallel, but **both must precede** any GEO-completeness work (H3) — optimising llms.txt while AI bots are blocked and content is JS-hidden would be measuring a closed shop. C2 and H2 are *outputs* of C3, so don't hand-fix them first if C3 is imminent.
